I don’t have live web access to read Namebeam’s 2026 pages, so I can’t look up that post and give you the exact number directly. If you can paste the record URL or the HTML for the 2026-09-01 → 2026-09-27 entries I’ll extract the domains and return the count.

Meanwhile, here are simple, copy-pasteable methods you can use to get the answer yourself.

1) Quick description of what to do
- Open Namebeam’s “AI Visibility Record” page (the page where the daily questions and answers are published).
- For each day from 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-27, find Perplexity’s answer block and collect all outbound links (hrefs).
- Extract the registered domain for each link (example: from https://example.subdomain.com/path → example.com).
- Count unique domains.
- Report the number and the Namebeam page URL where the record is published.

2) Python script (recommended)
- Install: pip install requests beautifulsoup4 tldextract
- Edit the script’s record_url variable to the Namebeam AI Visibility Record URL and run.

```python
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import tldextract

record_url = "https://namebeam.example/path-to-ai-visibility-record"  # <-- replace with the real URL

r = requests.get(record_url)
r.raise_for_status()
soup = BeautifulSoup(r.text, "html.parser")

# Heuristic: find elements that contain the word "Perplexity" (adjust selectors to the page structure)
perplexity_blocks = []
for tag in soup.find_all():
    if tag.string and "Perplexity" in tag.string:
        # take nearest ancestor that likely contains the answer (adjust as needed)
        ancestor = tag.find_parent(["article", "div", "section"]) or tag.parent
        if ancestor not in perplexity_blocks:
            perplexity_blocks.append(ancestor)

domains = set()
for block in perplexity_blocks:
    # restrict by date if the page contains dates — otherwise filter manually by block text containing the date range
    block_text = block.get_text()
    if any(d in block_text for d in ["2026-09-01","2026-09-02","2026-09-03","2026-09-04","2026-09-05",
                                     "2026-09-06","2026-09-07","2026-09-08","2026-09-09","2026-09-10",
                                     "2026-09-11","2026-09-12","2026-09-13","2026-09-14","2026-09-15",
                                     "2026-09-16","2026-09-17","2026-09-18","2026-09-19","2026-09-20",
                                     "2026-09-21","2026-09-22","2026-09-23","2026-09-24","2026-09-25",
                                     "2026-09-26","2026-09-27"]):
        for a in block.find_all("a", href=True):
            ext = tldextract.extract(a["href"])
            if ext.domain and ext.suffix:
                domains.add(f"{ext.domain}.{ext.suffix}")

print("Unique domains cited by Perplexity:", len(domains))
for d in sorted(domains):
    print(d)
print("Record URL:", record_url)
```

Notes:
- You may need to adjust how the script locates Perplexity answer blocks depending on the page’s DOM (look for a label/class like “source: Perplexity”, “answered by Perplexity”, or similar).
- If the record uses one page per date, loop over per-day URLs instead of a single record page and fetch each.

3) Shell one-liner (if the page is simple)
- Requires pup or htmlq to parse HTML and tldextract-like processing via awk/sed:
curl "https://namebeam.example/path" | pup 'a attr{href}' | sed -E 's@https?://([^/]+).*@\1@' | sed -E 's/^www\.//' | sort -u | wc -l
